messages:
Priya S.: Heads-up — proposing new SIEM export retention by environment: 90d for dev/staging exports, 365d for prod exports. Need security + legal signoff before we flip the pipeline. https://redwood-internal/docs/retention/siem-exports :thinking_face:
Alex K.: +1 on shorter dev retention. Question: do we still push raw payloads to S3 for dev, or keep only scrubbed views?
Priya S.: Plan is to keep raw in a 'tmp-raw' bucket for 7 days, then move to encrypted archive with limited access, but for dev we want no archive beyond 90d.
Marcus L.: Concern: exports currently unwrap using CMK for downstream partners. If we shorten prod retention to 365d we need a migration plan for key rotations and stored wrapped artifacts. Also how does this affect incident forensics?
Samir P.: Forensics note — we need a way to snapshot exports on-demand before retention TTL for legal holds. Should be an admin-only flow with audit and JIT KMS unwrap.
Legal Team: @Priya S. can you add a sample legal-hold workflow? We'll need hold triggers, retention freeze, and retention-owner contact info.
Priya S.: Yep; proposing an RFC doc section. Draft snippet: 
```
- Trigger: Security incident (INC-1234) or legal request
- Action: create hold ticket, snapshot export to hold-bucket, escalate KMS unwrap to 'forensics' role
- TTL: hold until released by Legal Team
```
Alex K.: RBAC change request: introduce a new role `siem_export_reader` that can read scrubbed exports but not unwrap CMK. `forensics_unwrap` role will be separate and require 2FA + manager approval. Thoughts?
Marcus L.: That separation looks good. We should enforce via an IAM condition: only allow decrypt if request has `project=forensics` and `approval=true`. Also log every unwrap with an immutable audit entry.
security-bot: Automated note — current SIEM exporter service account has decrypt permission on CMK `siem-export-key-v1`. Last change: 2025-11-03.
oncall: If we add JIT unwrap, make sure runbooks updated — oncall may need quick permissive path during active incident. Suggest an emergency bypass with post-hoc audit rather than full-time permission.
Samir P.: Implementation idea: use short-lived KMS grants (7d) tied to a ticket ID and deployed via a secure workflow (ticket -> approval -> grant). Grant metadata should include ticket id and approver.
Priya S.: OK — action items: 1) I'll update the RFC with retention matrix + legal-hold flow; 2) Alex to open RBAC PR for `siem_export_reader` and `forensics_unwrap`; 3) Marcus to propose KMS grant workflow; 4) Samir to draft runbook changes for incident response.
Alex K.: I'll open PR: PR-7890. Will include policy samples and least-privilege conditions.
Marcus L.: I'll prototype a lambda/orchestration job that attaches KMS grant to the unwrap call and writes an audit record to the immutable ledger.
Legal Team: We need timeline — can you target a 2-week review window? We have an external audit in ~3 weeks.
Priya S.: Two-week review works. I'll ping docs owners and schedule a short review session.
Alex K.: Quick sample IAM snippet I'll include in PR: 
```
- Effect: Allow
  Action: kms:Decrypt
  Resource: arn:aws:kms:...:siem-export-key-v1
  Condition:
    StringEquals:
      kms:GrantToken: "ticket-INC-1234"
```
Samir P.: +1. Also recommend masking highly sensitive PII at export time (hashing emails, masking IPs) — that reduces exposure and shortens forensic unwrap needs.
Marcus L.: Agree. Masking should be a configurable transform step in the export pipeline. We can ship default masks and allow opt-in raw export for approved forensics cases.
Priya S.: Great. If nobody objects, I'll file the RFC update today and tag reviewers. :thumbsup: 
Alex K.: No objections from me.
Marcus L.: Fine from infra side.
Legal Team: We'll review once RFC is up.
security-bot: Reminder — create a backlog ticket to remove any long-lived CMK grants. Found 2 grants older than 90 days: G-4433, G-4499.
Priya S.: Noted — adding cleanup task to action list.
Priya S.: Thanks everyone — will post the RFC link once live and schedule the review meeting.
